content.user_title: Design Clear Charts and Dashboard Layouts
content.value_statement: Choosing unsuitable charts can obscure comparisons, trends, and relationships. This skill recommends chart types and drafts configurations, styling guidance, and dashboard layouts for your audience.
actual_capabilities: Recommend chart types for comparisons, trends, distributions, proportions, relationships, and flows.
Draft ECharts configurations for bar, line, pie, and scatter charts.
Generate Chart.js configuration drafts with datasets, labels, colors, and responsive options.
Suggest dashboard layouts and Excel chart setup specifications.
Recommend professional, cool, warm, and colorblind-friendly color palettes.
Advise on axis scales, labels, units, typography, tooltips, and visual clarity.
limitations: Does not render charts directly; configurations need a separate charting tool.
Does not access your data directly; provide the relevant data or its structure.
Generated configurations may need adjustments for your library version and display environment.
Custom visualization types and real-time data require additional implementation.

use_cases.title: Compare Business Performance
use_cases.description: Select charts for regional sales comparisons and monthly trends, with clear labels and consistent scales.

use_cases.title: Draft Application Charts
use_cases.description: Generate ECharts or Chart.js configuration drafts from supplied categories, measures, and presentation requirements.

use_cases.title: Plan Executive Reports
use_cases.description: Outline dashboard layouts and Excel chart specifications that emphasize key metrics and readable summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a chart for comparing [measure] across [categories]. My audience is [audience]. Explain the choice and suggest axis labels.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an ECharts Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an ECharts configuration for [time periods] and [values]. Show the trend, label units, and recommend a readable palette.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Visualization Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [dataset], compare grouped bars, stacked bars, and line charts for [question]. Recommend one and draft its Chart.js configuration with consistent scales.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Dashboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a dashboard layout for [audience] using [metrics and datasets]. Recommend charts, ECharts configurations, accessible colors, interaction options, and implementation adjustments.

output_examples.input: Compare quarterly revenue for North, South, and West regions.
output: Recommended chart: Grouped bars with quarters on the horizontal axis and revenue on the vertical axis.
Use one consistent color per region and start the revenue axis at zero.
Label the currency and include a legend so readers can compare regions across quarters.

output_examples.input: Show how customer satisfaction relates to response time.
output: Recommended chart: Scatter plot with response time on the horizontal axis and satisfaction on the vertical axis.
Use a point for each observation and label both axes with their units.
Include tooltips for details and avoid presenting correlation as proof of causation.

output_examples.input: Plan an executive dashboard for monthly sales and regional performance.
output: Place the primary sales metric at the top, followed by a monthly trend line and a regional bar chart.
Keep region colors consistent and show units beside each measure.
Use concise titles and reduce gridlines so the main comparisons remain easy to read.

best_practices: Provide the data structure, analytical question, audience, and display context before requesting a design.
Use descriptive titles, labeled units, consistent comparison scales, and zero baselines for bar charts.
Test generated configurations in your target library and check contrast, labels, and accessibility.
anti_patterns: Expecting rendered charts or automatic access to private datasets from this instruction-only skill.
Forcing complex comparisons into crowded pie charts or using excessive colors.
Using generated configurations unchanged without checking library compatibility and data accuracy.

faq.question: Which charting libraries does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It provides configuration guidance for ECharts and Chart.js, plus Excel chart setup instructions.

faq.question: Can it render charts directly?
faq.answer: No. Use the generated configuration in a compatible charting tool or application.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your data or its structure, the question you need to answer, the audience, and the intended display format.

faq.question: Can it design dashboards?
faq.answer: It can suggest dashboard layouts and suitable charts. Building and connecting the dashboard requires separate implementation.

faq.question: Does it support accessible chart design?
faq.answer: It recommends colorblind-friendly palettes, clear labels, contrast checks, and alternative text considerations. Verify accessibility in the final rendered chart.

faq.question: Are generated configurations ready for every environment?
faq.answer: No. Adjust configurations for your charting library, data format, and application. Real-time data requires additional setup.
